name: pass-strength-hover-indicator

frames.best_why: Frame 5 shows the hover card with all five rules ticked alongside the filled strength bars.

tagline: A password box fills five green bars and explains the rules on hover.
summary: A password field with an eye toggle and five strength bars beneath it that fill as rules are met. An info icon beside the label opens a hover card listing each requirement with a tick or cross.
appearance: On a dark page, a labelled password input with an eye icon inside its right edge and a small coloured info dot at the top right. Below it run five short rounded segments that turn green as strength rises; an open hover card lists five green-ticked rules.
behaviour: Typing fills the bars one by one and recolours the info icon from red through green. Pointing at the icon opens a card that checks each rule live, and the eye button switches the field between hidden dots and plain text.
demo_content: Rules listed as At least 8 characters, 1 number, 1 lowercase, 1 uppercase and 1 special character.
search_phrases: signup password field with eye toggle
use_when: A sign-up or account form needs to guide people toward a stronger password as they type.
avoid_when: Rules live in a hover card only, so touch and keyboard users may not see why a password fails.
customise: The five rules and their patterns are a hardcoded array near the top, and the strength texts and colours sit in a config object. The field takes no props.
weight_why: One controlled input, five span bars and a small hover card.

a11y.note: The requirements only appear on hover, and the eye button hides its focus outline.

issues: One rule reads 'At least 1 special characters', which is ungrammatical.
The rules are only reachable through the hover card, so they are easy to miss on touch.
Strength bars carry no text, so colour alone signals how strong the password is.
polish_why: Clear strength feedback and tidy checks; small type and colour-only bars hold it back.
title: Password Strength Hover
